bridge_fqn_map.name: bridge_fqn_map.walk-dict-keys-not-values
bridge_fqn_map.what: Extends the traversal stack with a dict's KEYS (strings) instead of its VALUES. Strings never isinstance-match any tensor type, so every tensor nested under a mapping -- which is the entire sharded state dict -- is silently never visited, and the tool reports zero declared tensors without any exception being raised. On a real Bridge run this is exactly the vacuous-empty-map failure the tool exists to forbid, only now produced by the walker itself, and the count-mismatch against the checkpoint is the only evidence. Caught by: test_factory_tensors_are_declared_not_dropped

bridge_fqn_map.name: bridge_fqn_map.skip-tuple-containers
bridge_fqn_map.what: Recurses into lists but not tuples when walking the sharded state dict. Megatron state dicts freely nest tuples (a list of per-layer tuples is idiomatic), so every tensor sitting inside a tuple container is silently dropped from the declared set -- on the 26B that shape of nesting is what the vision-tower patch-embedder entry models. The walk completes normally, the file writes, the exit code is 0, and the only symptom is a map that under-declares tensors the save actually wrote, flipping their adjudication to undeclared. Caught by: test_factory_tensors_are_declared_not_dropped

bridge_fqn_map.name: bridge_fqn_map.objects-counted-as-tensors
bridge_fqn_map.what: Routes ShardedObject entries into the TENSOR set instead of the object set. Non-tensor state such as the TE ``linear_qkv._extra_state`` records then masquerade as declared tensors, inflating the declared-object count down to zero and claiming tensors the checkpoint never writes as tensors. The JSON still has the right shape and the run still exits 0; the map simply promises a disk entry for state that is not a tensor, so the downstream gate compares against a list that can never match a real save. Caught by: test_factory_tensors_are_declared_not_dropped

bridge_fqn_map.name: bridge_fqn_map.union-becomes-intersection
bridge_fqn_map.what: Accumulates per-chunk tensor keys by INTERSECTION instead of union. With the accumulator starting as the empty set, the very first chunk intersects to nothing, so a model built from any number of chunks -- one for non-pipelined, many for pipelined layouts -- always declares zero tensors. The defect only appears in the aggregation loop, the builder and walker are untouched, and an empty denominator is precisely the vacuity this tool was written to refuse, yet here it is manufactured silently after a fully successful model build.
